name: Hydration Checklist
description: A practical checklist of habits, warning signs and situations that help you stay properly hydrated through the day.

items.text: Drink a glass of water shortly after waking up
Keep a refillable water bottle within reach all day
Have a drink with every meal and snack
Sip steadily rather than gulping large amounts at once
items.note: Spreading intake through the day helps your body absorb fluids better.

items.text: Set a phone or watch reminder if you tend to forget
Eat water-rich foods like fruit, salad and soup
Check that your urine is pale yellow, not dark
Notice thirst and a dry mouth as early cues
Watch for headache, tiredness or trouble concentrating
Be alert to dizziness or feeling lightheaded when standing
For children and older adults, watch for fewer bathroom trips or confusion
items.note: These groups can dehydrate quickly and may not feel thirsty.

items.text: Increase fluids on hot or humid days, even without thirst
Carry extra water when spending time outdoors
Take shade and water breaks during peak heat
Watch for heavy sweating, cramps or feeling faint
items.note: These can signal heat-related illness that needs cooling and fluids.

items.text: Choose cool drinks and avoid excess alcohol in the heat
Drink water before you start a workout
Sip fluids during longer or more intense sessions
Rehydrate after exercising to replace what you lost
For long or sweaty sessions, consider an electrolyte drink
items.note: Plain water is enough for most everyday activity under an hour.

items.text: Weigh up the conditions: heat and humidity raise your needs
Add lemon, cucumber or berries to flavor water naturally
Keep a glass or bottle on your desk as a visual cue
Pair drinking with routines like meals or breaks
Choose a marked bottle to track how much you have had
Track your hydration habits with this printable checklist
Important: this is general information, not medical advice
items.note: If you have a condition affecting fluid intake or suspect serious dehydration, consult a doctor.

faq.q: How much water should I drink a day?
faq.a: A common guideline is around 6 to 8 cups of fluid a day, but needs vary with body size, activity, climate and health. Use thirst and pale yellow urine as everyday signs that you are drinking enough.

faq.q: What are the early signs of dehydration?
faq.a: Common signs include thirst, dry mouth, dark yellow urine, tiredness, headache, dizziness and reduced concentration. In young children and older adults, watch for fewer wet diapers or trips to the bathroom and confusion.

faq.q: Do drinks other than water count?
faq.a: Yes. Water is best, but milk, unsweetened tea, coffee in moderation and water-rich foods like fruit and soup all contribute to your fluid intake. Limit sugary and heavily caffeinated drinks.

faq.q: Can I print this hydration checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off your hydration habits and reminders throughout the day.
